body:
# Independent audit: variable density and intrinsic parity repair



* `candidate 93c94ac2c5c85584`;
* `candidate 1972e280d049f336`.

Both sources were read in full. The original continuous and mixed-fiber
selection proofs are dependencies, not repeated hypotheses. Neither
audited theorem proves OC.

## 1. Variable Borel densities

On an output fiber, partition the equality set of the inverse endpoint
map by its finitely many input-base values. The weighted area formula
on each such stratum gives exactly

    rho_p(A_q)<=integral_(T_i(A_q)) f_i(q,x)dx
              <=integral_(A_q) f_i(q,T_i(y)) |det DT_i(y)|dy.

This is in the correct direction even for noninjective T_i, since image
multiplicity is at least one. Nonnegative Borel weights suffice. Their
integrals may be infinite, but the inequality remains valid. Absolute
continuity of rho_p follows first by Lipschitz null-set preservation
and absolute continuity of the input measures. On the equality set the
weight f_i(F_i)|det DT_i| is finite almost everywhere, since f_i is
finite there and the derivative is finite almost everywhere. Thus the
measure comparison gives the asserted pointwise density inequality
without requiring bounded input reference densities.

The input marginal gives zero mass to {f_i=0}; its inverse-image under
F_i has zero output mass. The harmonic-power calculation can therefore
be performed where all endpoint ceilings are positive, as required by
the source's envelope hypothesis. At zero output density no further
argument is needed.

The same intrinsic slice matrices remain positive semidefinite in one
common conjugation, and their weighted sum is identity. Trace AM-GM
therefore yields the exact variable harmonic-power ceiling. The target
measure g sigma_P is explicitly assumed finite. It is a fixed finite
Borel measure on a compact metric space, hence a Radon measure; its
domination class is weakly closed by continuous tests. Consequently the
smooth-cost approximation and finite convex-test separation apply with
no regularity assumption on g beyond that in the source.

For one common positive density f, convexity of f^(-1/d) gives exactly
the needed envelope inequality, not its reverse. A positive log-concave
f satisfies this because the exponential of the convex function
-(log f)/d is convex. The one-dimensional cone reference 2r dr has
convex reciprocal 1/(2r) on its positive part. Its zero endpoint is
ignored only because it has zero marginal mass, not because an endpoint
atom is being deleted. This local profile result makes no comparison
between reference densities on different physical support faces.

## 2. Intrinsic parallelism within one parity class

For q>0, positive input mass in a fiber implies that its supporting
convex fiber has affine dimension q: a lower-dimensional fiber has zero
H_q measure. For every cross pair of positive input fibers in one
common parity class, convexity embeds their Minkowski midpoint in the
actual integer midpoint fiber. Two different q-dimensional direction
spaces would produce a Minkowski sum with dimension greater than q,
contradicting the definition of q. Fixing one positive fiber from each
side and comparing every cross pair proves a common direction space
for all positive input fibers in that class.

Orthogonal tangent coordinates preserve the H_q normalization. The
perpendicular offsets are legitimately finite auxiliary base coordinates,
because the mixed selection theorem allows arbitrary real finite bases.
If two input pairs at the same physical output base produced different
perpendicular offsets, their positive q-dimensional midpoint sets would
span dimension at least q+1 inside that one convex fiber. This is
impossible. Thus no hidden sum over auxiliary offsets inflates physical
fiber density.

For q=0 every fiber is a singleton and the entire set S is finite.
Treating the full physical points as auxiliary discrete bases is valid;
all product pairs within the original parity class still have actual
integer midpoint and lie in C. The discrete density bound is one per
physical point. No continuous dimension or 0^0 convention is used.

## 3. Marked-source lift

The old integer midpoint condition implies equality of the two endpoint
mass totals in each parity class. Each repaired class has the exact old
endpoint submarginals and dominates its old midpoint law in convex order.
The source's compact martingale-existence dependency therefore applies
classwise. Compose the old joint law of mark, parity, and midpoint with
that martingale, and then with the disintegration of the selected new
pair coupling over its midpoint.

The final drawn pair averages to that intermediate midpoint. The first
kernel's conditional mean is the old midpoint. The tower property gives
the exact old conditional midpoint mean for every source-mark/parity
row. Integrating removes the mark and returns the selected new coupling,
so both unconditional endpoint submarginals remain exact. The construction
does not preserve each marked row's separate endpoint means, and the
source correctly makes no such claim. The finite sum over parity classes
causes no measurable-selection problem.

## 4. Pointwise capacities and degeneracy factor

The compact attainable midpoint set D_r contains every selected class
output. Thus its density-one bound gives rho_r<=1_Dr mu and summing
gives the exact overlap-count ceiling. For upper-semicontinuous bounded
input ceilings, the harmonic-power mean extended by zero at a zero
argument is continuous and coordinatewise increasing. Compact maximizing
pair subsequences prove upper semicontinuity of c_r. The weighted
selection proof above applies on the augmented intrinsic coordinates.
Its maximum over base pairs within one class is legitimate; there is
no extra sum over those pairs.

For q<d, an integer base in the interior of the convex projection would
have a d-dimensional fiber: combine a lifted point beyond that base
along a segment with a small ambient ball at an interior point of C.
Thus all sampled bases lie on the projection's boundary. At any output
base p, a supporting affine functional forces both endpoints of a
midpoint pair into its supporting hyperplane A.

The lattice L=Z^n intersect direction(A) has rank r<=n-1 and is
saturated with respect to division by two. Hence the parity map on L
has kernel exactly 2L and image cardinality 2^r. The integer points
of A form one translate of L, so at most 2^(n-1) parity classes can
contribute at p. This establishes the claimed uniform degenerate
ceiling and the more precise local rank bound. The n=0 case cannot
have q<d for a full ambient convex body, so no negative exponent case
is hidden in the formulation.

## 5. Exact sharpness and affine-tilt limitations

For input bases {0,1}^n and {1,2}^n, an integer midpoint forces the
coordinate pairs (0,2) or (1,1). All outputs therefore have base
(1,...,1). Unit-density common convex continuous fibers give total
input and output mass 2^n in one volume-one output fiber. The common
continuous-point coupling attains this ceiling. This proves necessity
for every integer-output coupling, not just the selection construction.

The degenerate body in the source is convex, compact, and full ambient
dimensional: t can be strictly positive and less than epsilon<1, and
all |v| inequalities can then be strict. Its integer bases have t=0,
so its sampled fibers have exactly intrinsic dimension q. The remaining
n-1 base coordinates repeat the same forced-complement argument, proving
the sharp ceiling 2^(n-1). The proof includes n=1 and q=0, with the
stated counting normalization.

The affine-tilt counterexamples have the asserted unequal first moments
and masses; they correctly prevent importing convex order through an
unjustified change of measure. The literal closed-halfspace inequality
is pointwise on each endpoint pair. Combining it with the fixed class
mass and the capacity of the strict complement gives the displayed
positive-part cap payment. No halfspace order is inferred from convex
order, and no supporting first-variation allocation is silently equated
with a literal indicator.

## 6. Scope

The results provide exact intrinsic density repair, preserved marked
midpoint means, sharp global and local capacities, and actual tuple cap
credit. They neither select a deterministic OC center nor establish the
missing conversion from these measures to the exact halfspace-depth
constant. The simultaneous convex-order conclusion has one law for all
convex tests, while supporting allocations and cross-body conditional
surface-density compatibility remain separate requirements.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
